A 12-mile week where her legs only "came back by Thursday" reads like recovery after a race. The draft treats it that way. It turns down the jump to 40 miles, holds off speedwork until the week of Nov 9, and builds a gentle week of about 19 miles: all easy running with a heart-rate cap, rest on Monday and Friday, light strength and mobility on Wednesday instead of a session, and only a few relaxed strides on Saturday. That passes the safety checks on volume, long run and easing back after a marathon. The 6-mile Sunday run is modest, and the plan is clear enough to run day by day.

It answers both of her questions directly and honestly and reassures her that there's still time for the 10K. It doesn't invent a date for the 10K.

Two things keep it from a 5. The week-by-week table in the answers came out as broken plain-text lines, so the timeline to the 10K is hard to follow. The taper line ("wherever the Thanksgiving 10K falls") is also vague.
